title: Figma MCP Server
summary: Read Figma frames, variables and components through Figma's remote MCP server so generated UI code follows the real design.
description: Figma's MCP server hands an agent the structure behind a selected frame: layout, spacing, the variables and styles in use, and a screenshot for reference. Code written from that data is much closer to the design than code guessed from a description.

This setup uses the remote server at mcp.figma.com, so there is no app to run for the connection itself. You sign in with your Figma account, and the agent sees files that account can open. Paste a link to a frame in your prompt to point it at the right node.
useWhen: Build a component from a Figma frame link
Match spacing and colors to the design variables
Compare a coded screen against the design
Pull the design tokens a frame uses into a theme file

mcp.name: figma
access: Reads frames, components, variables and screenshots from Figma files your account can open
Uses your Figma sign-in; the agent can also upload generated images if asked

example.prompt: Implement the pricing card from this Figma frame as a React component using our Tailwind tokens: https://www.figma.com/design/abc123/Pricing?node-id=12-34
example.result: Read the frame: 3 text styles, 4 color variables, 24 px padding, 12 px radius. Created PricingCard.tsx using the matching Tailwind tokens and noted one color that has no token yet.

faq.question: Do I need the Figma desktop app?
faq.answer: Not for this remote URL. Figma also documents a desktop server, which this setup does not use.

faq.question: How do I sign in?
faq.answer: Your agent starts an OAuth login with Figma the first time it connects. Gemini CLI uses the /mcp auth figma command for this.

faq.question: How do I point it at one frame?
faq.answer: Include the frame link in your prompt. The link carries the node id the tools read.

access: Reads design data from Figma files you can open
